sections.content: How many people are "weighers, graders and sorters"?

6,740 people

were counted on the census as "weighers, graders and sorters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Weighers, graders and sorters weigh, grade and sort materials, goods and products.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "weighers, graders and sorters" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "weighers, graders and sorters", 12% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "weighers, graders and sorters" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "weighers, graders and sorters" included:

  • care workers and home carers
  • assemblers and routine operatives (other)
  • other administrative occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "weighers, graders and sorters" there were more men than women (60.6% compared with 39.4%).

This means "weighers, graders and sorters" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 60.6% and women made up 39.4% of "weighers, graders and sorters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "weighers, graders and sorters" included:

  • purchasing managers and directors
  • graphic and multimedia designers
  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "weighers, graders and sorters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "weighers, graders and sorters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "weighers, graders and sorters", 9.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (78.8% compared with 21.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.8%) than self-employed (3.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
